answer: A stake-or-bond rule makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it locks a bond that is slashed if it is caught running duplicate identities or cheating. Honest agents earn it back with interest, so a single real participant has little to lose, while an attacker spinning up a meadow of sock puppets must fund every one. Like boats tied at a jetty, each identity carries real collateral, and over the horizon the math turns against fraud: a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds, while honest work stays cheap.
